This round: invoicer/lines.py _rows reads with csv.reader(strict=True) and turns csv.Error into LineError `row N: a cell starts with a quotation mark but doesn't end with one that closes it; remove that mark, or end the cell with one and write each quotation mark inside it twice`, N being the row where the cell opens; command.py prints it after the file's path, exit 2, nothing on standard output. The parse_lines docstring Refuses names it. Tests: test_refuses_a_quotation_mark_that_never_closes_naming_the_row_where_it_opens and test_refuses_a_quotation_mark_that_never_closes_in_a_long_file and test_refuses_a_cell_with_text_after_its_closing_quotation_mark in tests/test_lines.py, test_refuses_a_quotation_mark_that_never_closes_naming_the_row_where_it_opens in tests/test_command.py. The other refusals (folder, unreadable file, number too large, more than three fields, empty description, heading row) stand in command.py and lines.py with their tests.

invoicer/command.py _rate: refuses a rate outside 0 to 100 and one above 0 and below 1, with or without %, asking for the percent; 0 gives no tax. Tests: test_refuses_a_rate_below_one_as_a_fraction, test_refuses_a_rate_below_one_written_with_a_percent_sign, test_takes_a_rate_of_zero, test_takes_a_rate_of_zero_written_with_a_percent_sign.

invoicer/command.py: --rate kept with action=append, and main refuses more than one with `the tax rate is given more than once; give it once, such as --rate 19`. Test: test_refuses_a_rate_given_twice.

more.where: invoicer/lines.py _rows: csv.reader(strict=True) raises where a quoted cell runs to the end of the text, and past 131072 characters raises for the cell's size, so neither a long file nor a short one reaches the caller as _csv.Error or as a later fault that hides the mark; both become the one LineError naming the row where the mark opens. Tried: a 30002-row and a 3-row file each exit 2 with that line and no traceback. Tests: test_refuses_a_quotation_mark_that_never_closes_in_a_long_file, test_refuses_a_quotation_mark_that_never_closes_naming_the_row_where_it_opens (lines and command).

settled.point: a cell with text after its closing quotation mark, such as "Pro" x;10.50;1
settled.decided: Refused with the same message as a mark that never closes, naming its row, where round 5 read it as Pro x
settled.ground: csv's strict mode, which the unclosed mark needs, also refuses it. It reads in no one way, a spreadsheet never saves it (it would save """Pro"" x"), and reading it as Pro x drops marks the colleague typed, so refusing it is what the decision a wrong line asks: no guess, one line saying what to fix. A mark inside a cell that doesn't start with one, such as 5" screen, still reads as typed (test_reads_a_quotation_mark_inside_a_cell_that_starts_without_one).

settled.decided: row N: a cell starts with a quotation mark but doesn't end with one that closes it; remove that mark, or end the cell with one and write each quotation mark inside it twice
settled.ground: One wording holds for both the mark that never closes and text after the closing mark, so the code reads no csv message text to tell them apart; it says where (the row where the cell opens), what is wrong, and the two ways to fix it, as code N8.5 asks.
